headline: Dr Alexey Kulikov: Air pollution should feature in type 2 diabetes prevention, citing umbrella review
dek: The WHO technical officer wrote on X that an umbrella review links long-term PM2.5 exposure to a higher risk of type 2 diabetes.
body:
Dr Alexey Kulikov, Technical Officer at the WHO Department of NCDs and Mental Health and part of the UN NCD Task Force Secretariat, wrote on X that air pollution should be considered part of diabetes prevention, not only a threat to the heart and lungs.

He pointed to a new umbrella review, the APEX-T2D study, which brought together 13 systematic reviews covering more than 200 million participant observations. According to Kulikov's post, long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) was associated with a 10–16% higher risk of type 2 diabetes for every 10 µg/m³ increase. He said the link held across the reviews and also appeared in areas with relatively low pollution. Exposure was further associated with higher blood sugar and related metabolic complications.

Kulikov wrote that the evidence comes from North America, Europe, East and South Asia, Latin America and Australia. He said the authors consider the findings most relevant to highly polluted South Asia, where diabetes rates are already high.

He added that because almost everyone breathes outdoor air pollution, even a modest rise in individual risk could add up to many extra cases worldwide. "Clean air is metabolic health policy too," he wrote.
key_quote: Clean air is metabolic health policy too.
